commits.message:
A Viewport keeps its scroll once the frame is drawn, not in render (rich-protocol-9xcs.399)

A render hands what it learned by drawing to its pass (afterPass in
src/core/protocol.ts), which runs it once the outermost render is drawn
whole; a measurement, a thrown pass and an abandoned one commit nothing.
Viewport resolves its offset purely and keeps it that way, so its state is
State and its render-purity debt row is gone. ListView and every per-frame
view show content through viewport.showing(content, follow?) instead of
assigning content and calling follow during the frame; follow() and the
content setter are removed.

Drain the render-purity allow-list (rich-protocol-9xcs.g0k) (#507)

* Drain the render-purity allow-list (rich-protocol-9xcs.g0k)

Every RENDER_PURITY_DEBT row is gone but Viewport's and TextInput's, which
rich-protocol-9xcs.399 and .o76 take.

- Tables, glyph sets, tokens and records are readonly types.
- No RegExp is held where the gate walks. `pattern` (src/core/pattern.ts)
  makes a held regex only from one without g or y and exposes only what
  never writes lastIndex; a scan builds its own g/y regex from the pattern's
  source. RegexHighlighter.highlights holds source and flags, all it reads.
- ListState joins State as a sanctioned holder: a list appended to in place,
  so Table.addRow, RichText spans and Console recording stay linear.
- Console, RichText, Layout, Live, Progress, Table, Column, Tree,
  ProgressBar, Spinner, MarkupRegistry, widget handler sets and the node
  traceback hook keep what changes after construction in a State; Rich's
  setters (tree.expanded, bar.completed, spinner.text, layout.visible,
  column.header/footer) stay, as accessors over it.
- table.columns is read-only and Column is a type-only export: nothing can
  push a hand-built column any more. Column's dead addCell/getCells go.
- EmbeddedText memoizes a reading's characters and spans, not a RichText,
  which a memo may not hold.

* Answer the high review of the render-purity drain (rich-protocol-9xcs.g0k)

- ListState.push takes one item: a rest parameter let Console spread a
  recording of any length into it and overflow the stack.
- RichText.append reads the appended spans before writing, so a text
  appended to itself ends.
- A table row keeps its section end in a State and a Progress keeps each
  task in one, so addSection and updateTask are O(1) again, not a copy of
  every row or task. A task's id is its place in the list.
- Every Console write is refused during a render it was not made in, so a
  print there fails alike whether the console records, captures or neither.
- markdown-parse reads an anchored pattern at an index from a slice instead
  of building a sticky regex per call, which had doubled parse time.
- nextUp is computed, not read through a buffer allocated per call.

* An onStyleError handler runs between passes (rich-protocol-9xcs.g0k)

Refusing every Console write during a render broke docs/style.md's
handler, which prints its report to a second console: a callback a render
makes to user code is an event handler, and protocol's betweenPasses runs
it as one.
Review: the template frames test names FrameSequence, not the removed Frames (rich-animation-27tq.0tc)

Review: the pulse test reads what Progress draws; one clock in the showcase (rich-animation-27tq.0tc)

The BarColumn pulse test supplied its own frame and compared against a
literal 7.5; it now prints the Progress and compares each row to the bar
drawn in a frame for 7.5s. A test pins that, in a frame of its own host,
a Progress holds what it would draw. Spinner's placed renderable is built
in the constructor after the sequences it closes over. The showcase draws
the dashboard at the Live's frame time, so the heading and the jobs share
one clock. Two doc sentences that described examples no longer present
are corrected.

An animation is drawn one way: placed (rich-animation-27tq.0tc)

Removes every public way to draw an animation at a time the caller names:
frameAt and its Stamped renderable, the Frames class, Spinner.drawnAt, and
ProgressBar's pulse: { t }, now pulse: true. A FrameSequence, a Spinner and a
pulse are placed and draw at the frame's time.

Progress draws its table in a frame of its own host's time when printed with
none, so the bars and spinners placed in it draw at the moment its tasks are
drawn at. Examples and docs place their animations; docs that played an effect
over frames at sampled moments now play it in a live fence.
